summary: Iter206 validates the SIMPLIFIED salary rule end-to-end: base_salary is ALWAYS monthly; period_type derives period amount (biweekly = /2, weekly = /4.33, monthly = full). base_salary_basis has no calculation effect anymore. Display-mode subtitle format = 'Monthly · Monthly payments · Biweekly: RD$37,500.00' (75000/2). Employee restored to base_salary=75000, payment_frequency=monthly per main-agent instructions.
action_items: None. Simplification is behaving as specified. Ready to promote to production.

people_ops.py:611 cost-centers aggregation uses raw $sum on base_salary. Verified 200.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Test file: /app/backend/tests/test_salary_simplified_monthly.py. To rerun: pytest backend/tests/test_salary_simplified_monthly.py -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/iter206_results.xml. Key endpoints: POST /api/people-ops/payroll/periods uses field names start_date/end_date/payment_date (NOT period_start/period_end/pay_date). The response of POST periods does NOT include entries inline — must fetch via GET /api/people-ops/payroll/periods/{period_id} which returns {..., entries: [...]}. Payroll projection GET /api/people-ops/payroll/projection?period_type=... returns {totals: {base_salary_period, ...}}. business_clarity reports return {records, summary, period}. Simplified salary rule: base_salary is monthly always; period math done in Python (÷2, ÷4.33, ×1). base_salary_basis field is deprecated — DB may still contain values but nothing reads it for calculations.
rca of the issue: Not a bug fix — this iteration validates a business-rule simplification. Previously (iter205) the aggregations and period math applied a $switch multiplier on base_salary_basis (biweekly ×2, weekly ×4.33). User requested to drop that entirely: 'salario mensual 22000, pago quincenal 11000 así debe ser la lógica.' Now base_salary is ALWAYS stored as the monthly amount, and period_type alone determines the period division. Migration ×2 (biweekly) and ×4.33 (weekly) was applied to legacy rows during main-agent step. Frontend basis dropdown removed, label updated to 'Salario Base Mensual', helper text explains the biweekly=÷2 rule with live preview. All 5 aggregations (people_ops stats/summary + cost-centers, business_clarity by-department + by-cost-center + budget-alerts) confirmed reverted to raw $sum. All 12 test cases green.
